text: Before any work on an issue, search PRs (open and closed) that mention its number; someone may have fixed it already.
Before writing 'here's why', search the repo that owns the cause for the exact function or pattern name.
For 'version X broke it' reports, diff the published packages for X-1 and X before building a reproduction.
Write the failing script first and run it at the reported version. A repro that never failed proves nothing.
A passing check tells you about the check. After the checks, ask once whether it actually works for the person, and answer with the object.
Test in the place it runs (shallow clone, released version, their CI settings), not only where you built it.
Before saying 'X hangs/fails', copy the project's addopts at the release tag and check your own timeout and setup.
Runners record rc, seconds and maxrss per unit; read sort-by-maxrss first. A unit with no summary line was probably killed.
Don't browse 'good first issue' labels; run the project's own test suite and look at what breaks.
Read the project's contributing page and AI policy before you run anything, then run tests, then write up, then post.
Count helpers already on the bug and maintainers available to read; too many of one or too few of the other means you're extra work.
Count what a finding costs the reader to take. Post the smallest true thing, with the exact version that fixes it.
Is it alive in 2026, from a dated 2026 source? A fact on screen that says 'gone' is a finding, not background.
Before pricing anything: does the platform forbid it, does someone give it away, is the name taken?
